texts: DualKnife J retains the small knife diameter and disk-shaped tip of DualKnife, with cutting and hooking ability described as comparable. It has the same sheath diameter as DualKnife, allowing suction alongside the knife when inserted in the forceps channel.

The source describes DualKnife and DualKnife J as sharing three features: a flexible sheath, easiness of handling the knife, and stable handling provided by a disk-tipped knife and a rounded sheath tip. It states that together these allow the operator to incise and dissect in any direction at a stable speed while a constant depth is maintained. For DualKnife J specifically it states that a water jet function has been added, so that the device can deal with almost all steps involved in ESD, and that changing devices for submucosal injections is no longer necessary.

In the open-surgery instrument handling text, Mayo scissors are described as heavier surgical scissors used for cutting sutures, clothes, and fascia. The source gives no blade shape, tip geometry, length or color details.

Mayo scissors are described as heavy scissors available in multiple varieties. The source states straight scissors are used for cutting suture ("suture scissors"), while curved scissors are used for cutting heavy tissue such as fascia.

The supplied block (p1_b7) states institutional eligibility criteria for performing ESD at Keio University Hospital: absence of lymph node metastasis risk, lesion approachability, assured patient safety with Surgical Department backup during and after the procedure, performance regardless of tumor size or treatment history, and multidisciplinary conference consultation. These are purely institutional eligibility and case-selection policies, not visual evidence criteria.
